text:
Ivar Stenberg went second overall in June, one pick after Gavin McKenna, and 19 games in he's doing what top picks are supposed to do: producing on a bad team. He has 11 points, five goals, eight of those points on the power play, and he scored again Saturday in Dallas. Every forward picked in the top four since 2005 who stuck around reached 200 NHL games, and their median first full season was 0.56 points a game. He's at 0.58.

The caution is five on five. San Jose has taken just 38% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and his shooting percentage (17.9%) is above where we expect it to land. He also lost his spot on the first power-play unit to Michael Misa recently. None of that is unusual for a teenager on a team that has lost seven of eight.

Our range is wide, as it should be: 36 to 63 points over a full season. Tonight he's one of our Sleepers against the Islanders: his shots have been dangerous lately, and we have him at 22% to score.
headline: Stenberg is right on schedule
